landability_note: Backend-only Rust edit confined to a single api-server service file (workflow_executor.rs), no migration and no client/openapi regen. Verifiable via `cargo build -p api-server` plus a focused unit test: two workflows subscribed to one event where the first has a malformed stored condition JSON, asserting the second still executes. Remedy: scope the condition-evaluation error to the single workflow (log against the offending workflow_id and `continue`, matching the existing execute_workflow Err arm at :395-402) instead of `?`-propagating out of the whole batch.

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:348-403 — process_event loads every workflow subscribed to an event and iterates `for workflow in workflows`. Inside the loop (line 359) it evaluates each workflow's stored conditions with `if !self.evaluate_conditions(&conditions, &context)? { ... continue; }`. The `?` propagates a WorkflowError out of the ENTIRE batch function, aborting processing of every remaining subscribed workflow for that event.

evaluate_conditions returns Err(WorkflowError::ConditionError(...)) on a malformed/undeserializable stored condition (e.g. workflow_executor.rs:523 and :793). Conditions are author-supplied JSON persisted on the workflow row (`workflow.conditions.0`), so schema drift, a renamed operator, or any serde-shape change in ONE workflow makes evaluate_conditions return Err and, via the `?` at line 359, silently suppresses ALL other workflows triggered by the same event.

Asymmetry confirming this is a bug, not intent: the execute_workflow failure arm in the SAME loop (lines 395-402) correctly ISOLATES a failure — it logs `warn!(workflow_id, error, "Failed to start workflow execution")` and continues to the next workflow. The condition-evaluation path at line 359 does not get the same isolation, so a condition error has strictly larger blast radius (whole batch) than an execution error (one workflow).

Dedup/tracking status: this finding was first emitted as id code-review-api-core-workflow-condition-err-aborts-batch in signals/2026-10-01-api-core-tier1d.json, but that id is ABSENT from .research/backlog.json items (verified by id-keyed scan) — it was never reconciled into a tracked backlog row. The bug is still live: `sed -n '359p'` on 2026-10-21 still shows `if !self.evaluate_conditions(&conditions, &context)? {`. Re-emitted under the same id to re-assert an untracked, still-unfixed finding into the starved claim buffer; an id-keyed reconcile will upsert rather than duplicate.

Severity MEDIUM (+2): no data loss and no crash of the process (Axum/worker isolates the task), but a single org-authored malformed condition silently disables every other automation on that event type until the bad condition is corrected — a reliability/availability gap on a side-effecting automation surface (workflows send email/notifications and make outbound api_call requests). Confidence medium: the propagation path is confirmed by static read; whether a malformed stored condition currently exists in production is data-dependent, so the trigger is latent rather than runtime-confirmed.
